exposure: latency interval between antenatal corticosteroid administration and delivery
outcome: neonatal hypoglycemia (<40 mg/dL within 24 hours of life)
cohort: The study included 812 pregnant women (406 exposed to antenatal corticosteroids and 406 unexposed) between 34 0/7 and 36 6/7 weeks of gestation.
finding: The risk of neonatal hypoglycemia is greatest in the latency period of 12 to 71 hours between steroid administration and delivery in late preterm neonates, with the highest risk observed 24 to 47 hours after administration.
